topic: Abstract Vector Spaces: Beyond the Arrow

sections.title: The Familiar: Vectors as Geometric Arrows
lecture_lines: Traditionally, we visualize vectors as arrows in space.
An arrow has both a magnitude and a direction.
We add vectors by placing them tip-to-tail.
Multiplying by a scalar stretches or shrinks the arrow.
In geometry, vectors represent physical movement or force.
animations: Show a coordinate plane with a green (#00FF00) vector arrow from (0,0) to (3,2). Label it 'v'.
Place a yellow (#FFFF00) vector starting at (3,2) and ending at (4,3). Show the resulting sum vector in white (#FFFFFF) from (0,0) to (4,3).
Take a magenta (#FF00FF) vector at (1,0.5). Scale it by factor 2, showing it stretch to (2,1). Label the scale '2v'.

sections.title: The Leap: What is 'Abstract'?
lecture_lines: Modern math defines vectors by behavior, not appearance.
Any set following specific rules forms a vector space.
We move from "what it is" to "how it behaves".
animations: Morph a geometric arrow into a 2x2 grid representing a grayscale digital image. Label it 'Digital Vector'.
Show two 2x2 grids (images) with different intensities. Add them to create a third grid with combined intensities.
Display a set boundary (circle) containing both arrows and image grids. Label the set 'Vector Space' in light blue (#ADD8E6).

sections.title: The 8 Golden Rules (Axioms)
lecture_lines: To qualify, a set must obey ten strict axioms.
Closure ensures results stay within the same set.
Every space needs a zero vector as an origin.
Every element must have an additive inverse.
These rules create a consistent mathematical playground.
animations: Display a checklist [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/checklist.svg] with '8 Axioms' title. The first item 'Closure' highlights in gold (#FFD700).
Animate two dots inside a circular boundary (#0000FF). A plus sign joins them, and the result remains inside the circle.
Show a vector 'v' and its mirror '-v' in red (#FF0000). They move together and vanish into a '0' symbol at the center.

sections.title: A Non-Geometric World: Function Spaces
lecture_lines: Functions can be treated exactly like geometric vectors.
Adding two functions produces another valid function.
This proves that "vectors" can be wavy curves.
animations: Plot two polynomial curves: f(x)=x^2 in cyan (#00FFFF) and g(x)=x in orange (#FFA500) on a dark grid.
Animate the point-wise addition of the two curves to form a new curve h(x)=x^2+x in white (#FFFFFF).
Highlight the cyan curve f(x) and scale its y-values by 0.5, showing the curve flattening. Label it '0.5 * f(x)'.

sections.title: Dimension and Basis: The DNA of the Space
lecture_lines: A basis is a set of fundamental building blocks.
Every vector is a unique combination of basis elements.
Basis vectors must be linearly independent from each other.
The number of basis vectors defines the dimension.
These coordinates allow us to navigate abstract spaces.
animations: Show three base circles: Red (#FF0000), Green (#00FF00), and Blue (#0000FF). Label them 'Basis' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/basis.svg].
Animate sliders next to each color. As sliders move, a central 'Result' circle changes color to Purple (#800080).
Display the text 'Dimension = 3' in light grey (#D3D3D3) as the three basis elements are highlighted one by one.

sections.title: The Power of Abstraction: Real-world AI
lecture_lines: Artificial intelligence treats data points as abstract vectors.
Word embeddings map meanings into high-dimensional space.
Vector math helps machines understand similarities in data.
animations: Animate a voice waveform (#00FF00) flowing from a microphone [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/microphone.svg] into a vertical list of numbers (a vector).
Show a 2D cloud of points. A new point 'Input' appears in yellow (#FFFF00) in the middle of the cloud.
Draw a line from the 'Input' point to the nearest cluster of points labeled 'Matches'. The match glows white (#FFFFFF).
